sentences.text: This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. by accused No.2 in Cr.No.159/2023 of Marathahalli Police Station, registered for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 306 r/w Section 34 of IPC.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned HCGP for the State and perused the records of the case.
3.
The learned HCGP has filed statement of objections.

4. The first informant's sister by name Smt. Ashwini committed suicide by hanging herself in her house situated at No.1293, Mirchi Marathahalli, Bangalore, on 19.06.2022 at about 8.00 p.m.
leaving behind a death note written in her dairy.

Based on the complaint, the aforementioned case was registered against her husband and the petitioner herein, operator of one TSI Solutions, NC:
2023:KHC:25394 wherein the deceased was working.
The petitioner was arrested on 20.06.2023 and he is in judicial custody.
5. As per the complaint averments, accused No.1 namely the husband of the deceased since marriage, was harassing the deceased.

Her brother and parents were advising them to live cordially,
but even after the birth of a child, deceased was being harassed by her husband and he was not getting involved in the family emotionally and financially.
The allegations against the present petitioner is that even after the deceased handed over her resignation, he did not accept it and he was torturing her without releasing her from duty.

It is further alleged that the deceased was working for more than 12 hours and the petitioner was making her to work from his home office without giving any sick leave etc.,
6.
The learned counsel for petitioner would point out that though the deceased had submitted the resignation letter, she had withdrawn the same by sending an email on 03.06.2023.

He contends that there is no NC: 2023:KHC:25394 specific allegation against the petitioner that he has subjected the deceased to physical or mental harassment or intentionally aided her to commit suicide.

7. The learned HCGP contends that the investigation is in progress and in view of the death note,
there is a prima facie case against the petitioner.
He contends that the petitioner has abetted the deceased to commit suicide by his conduct and therefore, seeks to reject the petition.

sentences.text: At this stage, the allegations made against the petitioner is not sufficient to hold that the petitioner has intentionally instigated or abetted the deceased to commit suicide.
The ingredients of the offence alleged against the petitioner have to be established during a full-fledged trial.
It is contended by the learned counsel for petitioner that the deceased though submitted her resignation,
has later requested to withdraw the same, which shows that there was no harassment meted to her.
The petitioner is already arrested and interrogated.
He is not required for any further interrogation.
His further detention in custody is not required.
Hence, by imposing suitable conditions, the relief sought by the petitioner can be granted.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER I) The petition is allowed.
II) Petitioner/accused No.2 in Cr.No.159/2023 of Marathahalli Police Station,
Bangalore City shall be enlarged on bail subject to following conditions.
i) He shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with two sureties for the like-sum to the satisfaction of Jurisdictional Court.
ii) He shall furnish proof of his residential address and furnish his contact number and shall inform the Court, if there is any change in the address or contact number.

iii) He shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses/evidence in any manner.
iv) He shall not indulge himself in any criminal activities.
NC: 2023:KHC:25394 v) He shall appear before the trial Court on every date of hearing without fail.
Sd/-
